title: Major scales and intervals
summary: Build major scales from whole and half steps, play C, G, D, and F major with thumb crossings, and name intervals.

lessons.title: The major scale formula
lessons.summary: Every major scale follows the same pattern of whole and half steps.

steps.title: A pattern of steps
steps.body:
A **scale** is a set of notes played in order from one note up to the same note an octave higher. The first note is the **tonic**, and it names the scale.

Every **major scale** uses the same pattern of steps:

**W W H W W W H** (W = whole step, H = half step)

Starting on C, that pattern uses only white keys: C D E F G A B C. The half steps fall at E–F and B–C.

diagram.caption: C major, numbered by scale degree.

steps.title: Scale degrees
steps.body:
Each note of a scale has a number called its **scale degree**: in C major, C = 1, D = 2, E = 3, F = 4, G = 5, A = 6, B = 7, then C = 1 (or 8) again. Degree numbers let you talk about any key the same way: "the 5th degree" is G in C major and D in G major.

The half steps in a major scale are always between degrees **3–4** and **7–8**.

questions.prompt: What is the step pattern of a major scale?
choices: W W H W W W H
W H W W H W W
W W W H W W H
H W W W H W W
questions.explanation: Whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.

questions.prompt: In a major scale, the half steps fall between degrees…
questions.explanation: In C major: E–F (3–4) and B–C (7–8).

questions.prompt: What is the 5th degree of C major?
questions.explanation: C D E F G: G is 5.

questions.prompt: The first note of a scale is called the…
questions.explanation: The tonic is the home note that names the scale.

reviewItems.answer: W W H W W W H

reviewItems.prompt: Between which degrees are the half steps in a major scale?

lessons.title: C major with thumb crossings
lessons.summary: Play eight notes with five fingers by passing the thumb under and crossing over.

steps.title: Thumb under, finger over
steps.body:
A scale has eight notes but you have five fingers, so the hand has to move without a gap in the sound.

**Right hand, C major, one octave (C4 to C5):**
- Up: **1 2 3 1 2 3 4 5**. After finger 3 plays E, the **thumb passes under** to play F.
- Down: **5 4 3 2 1 3 2 1**. After the thumb plays F, **finger 3 crosses over** to play E.

Keep the thumb moving under the hand early, while fingers 2 and 3 are still playing, so it is ready. Keep the wrist level and let the elbow move sideways slightly; do not twist the wrist.

diagram.caption: RH fingering up: C1 D2 E3 F1 G2 A3 B4 C5.

exercise.prompt: Thumb-under drill, right hand: C4 D4 E4 F4 (1 2 3 1), then back E4 D4 C4 (3 2 1). Repeat slowly.
exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q h

mistakeTips: Start moving the thumb toward F while finger 2 plays D.
The thumb plays on its side; do not rotate the whole hand.
Aim for an even sound with no gap at the crossing.

exercise.prompt: Right hand, C major scale, C4 to C5 and back. Fingering up 1 2 3 1 2 3 4 5, down 5 4 3 2 1 3 2 1.
exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q q q q q q q q q h

mistakeTips: The thumb passes under after E (finger 3) going up.
Finger 3 crosses over the thumb to E going down.
If a note is late at the crossing, slow the tempo rather than rushing the other notes.

steps.title: Left hand, C major
steps.body:
**Left hand, one octave (C3 to C4):**
- Up: **5 4 3 2 1 3 2 1**. After the thumb plays G, **finger 3 crosses over** to A.
- Down: **1 2 3 1 2 3 4 5**. After finger 3 plays A, the **thumb passes under** to G.

Notice the left hand's fingering going up matches the right hand's going down.

diagram.caption: LH fingering up: C5 D4 E3 F2 G1 A3 B2 C1.

exercise.prompt: Left hand, C major scale, C3 to C4 and back. Fingering up 5 4 3 2 1 3 2 1, down 1 2 3 1 2 3 4 5.
exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q q q q q q q q q h

mistakeTips: Finger 3 crosses over the thumb from G to A going up.
Going down, the thumb passes under after A.
Keep the left wrist from collapsing inward at the crossing.

questions.prompt: Right hand C major going up: which finger plays F?
questions.explanation: 1 2 3 1 2 3 4 5: the thumb passes under to F.

questions.prompt: Right hand C major going down: which finger plays E after the thumb plays F?
questions.explanation: Finger 3 crosses over the thumb.

questions.prompt: Left hand C major going up: which finger plays A?
questions.explanation: 5 4 3 2 1 then 3 crosses over to A.

questions.prompt: Left hand C major going up: which finger plays C4 at the top?
questions.explanation: 5 4 3 2 1 3 2 1: the thumb ends on C4.

reviewItems.prompt: Right-hand C major fingering going up?
Left-hand C major fingering going up?

lessons.title: G major and D major
lessons.summary: Add sharps to keep the major pattern, using the same fingering as C.

steps.title: Why G major needs F♯
steps.body:
Apply **W W H W W W H** from G: G–A (W), A–B (W), B–C (H), C–D (W), D–E (W), E–**F♯** (W), **F♯**–G (H).

Using F natural would put a half step at E–F and a whole step at F–G, breaking the pattern. So **G major = G A B C D E F♯ G**, with one sharp.

**Fingering is the same as C major** in both hands: RH up 1 2 3 1 2 3 4 5; LH up 5 4 3 2 1 3 2 1. In the right hand, finger 4 plays F♯.

exercise.prompt: Right hand, G major, G4 to G5 and back. Fingering up 1 2 3 1 2 3 4 5.
exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q q q q q q q q q h

mistakeTips: F♯5 is the black key just below G5; finger 4 plays it.
The thumb passes under to C5 after B4.
Keep finger 4 close to the black key before you need it.

exercise.prompt: Left hand, G major, G2 to G3 and back. Fingering up 5 4 3 2 1 3 2 1.
exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q q q q q q q q q h

mistakeTips: Finger 3 crosses over to E3 after the thumb plays D3.
Finger 2 plays F♯3.
G2 is low: play firmly so the microphone hears it.

steps.title: D major: two sharps
steps.body:
From D: D–E (W), E–**F♯** (W), F♯–G (H), G–A (W), A–B (W), B–**C♯** (W), C♯–D (H).

**D major = D E F♯ G A B C♯ D**, with two sharps: F♯ and C♯.

**Fingering is again the same as C major**: RH up 1 2 3 1 2 3 4 5 (finger 3 on F♯, 4 on C♯); LH up 5 4 3 2 1 3 2 1.

exercise.prompt: Right hand, D major, D4 to D5 and back. Fingering up 1 2 3 1 2 3 4 5.
exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q q q q q q q q q h

mistakeTips: Finger 3 is on F♯4, a black key, before the thumb passes under to G4.
Finger 4 plays C♯5.
Play slightly nearer the black keys so you do not have to reach.

exercise.prompt: Left hand, D major, D3 to D4 and back. Fingering up 5 4 3 2 1 3 2 1.
exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q q q q q q q q q h

mistakeTips: Finger 3 plays F♯3, then 2 on G3, 1 on A3.
Finger 3 crosses over to B3; finger 2 plays C♯4.

questions.prompt: Which note is sharp in G major?
questions.explanation: E–F♯ must be a whole step and F♯–G a half step.

questions.prompt: Which notes are sharp in D major?
questions.explanation: D E F♯ G A B C♯ D.

questions.prompt: The right-hand fingering for G major and D major is the same as for…
questions.explanation: C, G, and D major all use RH 1 2 3 1 2 3 4 5.

questions.prompt: Which note is the 7th degree of G major?
questions.explanation: G A B C D E F♯: F♯ is 7.

reviewItems.answer: G A B C D E F♯ G
D E F♯ G A B C♯ D

lessons.title: F major: finger 4 on B♭
lessons.summary: A scale with a flat, and a right-hand fingering that differs from C.

steps.title: Why F major needs B♭
steps.body:
From F: F–G (W), G–A (W), A–**B♭** (H), B♭–C (W), C–D (W), D–E (W), E–F (H).

**F major = F G A B♭ C D E F**, with one flat, B♭. (It is written B♭, not A♯, because a scale uses each letter once.)

steps.title: F major fingering
steps.body:
- **Right hand up: 1 2 3 4 1 2 3 4.** Finger 4 plays B♭, then the thumb passes under to C. Down: 4 3 2 1 4 3 2 1.
- **Left hand up: 5 4 3 2 1 3 2 1** (same as C major). The thumb plays C, then finger 3 crosses over to D. Down: 1 2 3 1 2 3 4 5.

The right hand avoids putting the thumb on the black key B♭, which would be awkward.

diagram.caption: RH: F1 G2 A3 B♭4 C1 D2 E3 F4.

exercise.prompt: Right hand, F major, F4 to F5 and back. Fingering up 1 2 3 4 1 2 3 4, down 4 3 2 1 4 3 2 1.
exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q q q q q q q q q h

mistakeTips: Finger 4 plays B♭4; the thumb passes under to C5.
Going down, finger 4 crosses over the thumb from C5 to B♭4.
Do not start with the thumb on B♭.

exercise.prompt: Left hand, F major, F3 to F4 and back. Fingering up 5 4 3 2 1 3 2 1.
exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q q q q q q q q q h

mistakeTips: Finger 2 plays B♭3, the thumb plays C4, then finger 3 crosses over to D4.
Down: after D4 (3), the thumb passes under to C4.

questions.prompt: Which note is flat in F major?
questions.explanation: A–B♭ is the half step between degrees 3 and 4.

questions.prompt: Right hand F major going up: which finger plays B♭?
questions.explanation: 1 2 3 4 1 2 3 4: finger 4 plays B♭.

questions.prompt: Why is it B♭ and not A♯ in F major?
choices: Each letter is used once in the scale
A♯ is a different key on the piano
questions.explanation: F G A B♭ uses each letter once. A♯ would repeat A and skip B.

questions.prompt: Left-hand F major fingering going up is…
questions.explanation: The left hand uses the same fingering as C major.

reviewItems.answer: F G A B♭ C D E F

reviewItems.prompt: Right-hand F major fingering going up?

lessons.title: Intervals: measuring distance
lessons.summary: Name the distance between two notes by number and quality, and hear them.

steps.title: Interval number
steps.body: An **interval** is the distance between two notes. Its **number** comes from counting letter names, **including both ends**: C to E is C-D-E = a **3rd**; C to G is C-D-E-F-G = a **5th**. The same letter is a **unison**; the next same letter up is an **octave** (8th).

steps.title: Interval quality
steps.body:
The **quality** tells you the exact size in half steps:

| Interval | Half steps | Example from C |
|---|---|---|
| minor 2nd (m2) | 1 | C–D♭ |
| major 2nd (M2) | 2 | C–D |
| minor 3rd (m3) | 3 | C–E♭ |
| major 3rd (M3) | 4 | C–E |
| perfect 4th (P4) | 5 | C–F |
| tritone (A4/d5) | 6 | C–F♯ / C–G♭ |
| perfect 5th (P5) | 7 | C–G |
| minor 6th (m6) | 8 | C–A♭ |
| major 6th (M6) | 9 | C–A |
| minor 7th (m7) | 10 | C–B♭ |
| major 7th (M7) | 11 | C–B |
| perfect octave (P8) | 12 | C–C |

From the tonic of any major scale, every scale degree is a major or perfect interval: M2, M3, P4, P5, M6, M7, P8.

steps.title: Hearing intervals
steps.body:
Link each interval to the start of a tune you know (all public domain):

- **M2**: "Frère Jacques" (first two notes)
- **m3**: "Greensleeves" (first two notes)
- **M3**: "When the Saints Go Marching In" ("Oh when")
- **P4**: Wagner's "Here Comes the Bride" ("Here comes")
- **P5**: "Twinkle, Twinkle" ("twinkle, twin-")
- **M6**: "My Bonnie Lies Over the Ocean" ("My Bon-")
- **P8**: the same note, higher; the two blend almost into one sound.

steps.title: Major and perfect intervals above C
steps.caption: C–D, C–E, C–F, C–G, C–A, C–B, C–C.

exercise.prompt: Listen to the interval, then play both notes, lower first. This one starts on C4.

mistakeTips: Count letter names to find the upper note: for a 5th, count C D E F G.
Sing the two notes before you play them.
Replay the example as many times as you like.

exercise.prompt: Listen, then play it back starting on C4.

mistakeTips: This is a 3rd: count C D E.
A major 3rd is 4 half steps.

exercise.prompt: Listen, then play it back starting on G4.

mistakeTips: This is a 4th: count G A B C.
A perfect 4th is 5 half steps.

questions.prompt: C to A is what interval?
questions.explanation: C D E F G A = 6 letters; 9 half steps = major 6th.

questions.prompt: How many half steps are in a perfect 5th?
questions.explanation: C–G spans 7 half steps.

questions.prompt: D to F is what interval?
questions.explanation: D E F = 3rd; D–F is 3 half steps, so minor.

questions.prompt: E to A is what interval?
questions.explanation: E F G A = 4th; 5 half steps = perfect.
